source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure's four 15-minute phases equal one hour per block size and repeat over nine sizes, yielding nine hours, while Machine Time is 1080 minutes (18 hours). The source also says all SSDs but supplies no population or per-device mapping. Timing changes endurance and coverage and requires an owner ruling; population is a mandatory execution input while Master remains unchanged.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The E1.S concurrent-stress objective is clear enough to govern once timing and population are ruled and safe per-device ranges are supplied, so execution is conditional REQUIRES rather than irreducibly BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Separates every E1.S device's evidence, exposes the nine-versus-18-hour conflict, and prevents one hardcoded namespace from standing in for destructive simultaneous population coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: Concurrent NVMe stress is not merely several independent jobs: devices can share PCIe switches, airflow and power rails, so one target's thermal throttling or link reset can disturb the whole set. Acceptance therefore needs both per-device health/integrity and a synchronized aggregate timeline. The literal phase arithmetic is nine hours; doubling exposure to match the machine estimate cannot be assumed because it changes endurance and shared-resource risk.
